correctness.rationale: The circular midpoint matrix has complex eigenvalues e^{pi ir/n}cos(pi r/n); after removing the constant mode the r=±1 pair dominates for fixed n, yielding a principal harmonic ellipse A e^{it}+B e^{-it} with semiaxes |A|+|B|, ||A|-|B||. For n independent arclength-uniform circle points ordered by increasing polar angle, write U_(j)=j/n+D_j. The empirical quantile functional CLT gives sqrt(n)D_j=>-Brownian bridge; Taylor expansion of exp(2pi i U_(j)) and the vanishing sum of second Fourier roots yield sqrt(n) B=> (1/2)int_0^1 exp(4pi it)dW(t). Real and imaginary parts each have variance 1/8, so P(|G|>r)=exp(-4r²). Meanwhile A->1; consequently sqrt(n)(1-b/a)=>2|G| with CDF 1-exp(-x²), and n^{1/4} e=>2sqrt(|G|) with CDF 1-exp(-x^4/4). The circle rotation symmetry (including any cyclic relabel) rotates the ellipse as a SET and preserves semiaxes; conditional Haar invariance makes the axis angle exactly uniform and independent for each finite n. Zero/degenerate coefficients are analytic nullsets. An independent 12000-sample finite n=256 diagnostic obtained P(H<1)=0.6571 versus limit 0.6321, within a finite-size tolerance; it is NOT the quantile-process proof. The limit order is k→∞ for each fixed n, then n→∞; no simultaneous interchange.
